__note: Question -> exemplar SQL, seeded from api/services/ai/semantics.md AND NOWHERE ELSE.
NO SQL LIVES IN THIS FILE. Each entry names a section and the index of the ```sql
block inside it; the SQL is read from semantics.md at load. That file is already
runtime (load_semantics renders it into the system prompt) and every block in it is
already executed with LIMIT 1 under jigged_ai_readonly on every CI run by
test_ai_read_access.py::test_every_reference_query_in_semantics_runs. Copying the
queries here would create a second source of truth for SQL that the repo executes
from exactly one place, and only one of the two copies would be checked.
NEVER HAND-AUTHOR AN EXEMPLAR FOR AN EVAL QUESTION. Three of the eleven eval
questions -- work centre queue, quoted-last-month-versus-prior, parts with no
routing -- have no reference query in semantics.md, and they STAY exemplar-free.
They are the within-experiment control: three questions in the same run, same
model, same pipeline, with nothing retrieved. Writing pairs for them would delete
the only part of the run that measures the pipeline without retrieval's help.
The payroll question likewise has no pair and must decline.
source_question IS AN EXACT KEY, NOT A LABEL. Leave-one-out excludes on this
string, so for a pair that answers an eval question it is that question verbatim.
The three pairs whose source_question is not an eval question are distractors in
the index -- which is what makes the floor measurement mean anything.
ALIASES ARE SCORED, NOT DISPLAYED. A pair's score is the max cosine over its
canonical question and its aliases, which is what lifts a real shop phrasing
('how many jobs are overdue') over the floor without dropping the floor for
everyone. A phrasing used as a test paraphrase must NOT appear here, or the test
measures string identity instead of retrieval.

AN ALIAS CAN RE-OPEN A TRAP THE FLOOR WAS SET TO CLOSE, and one did. cost_and_gross_profit carried 'how much margin are we making on jobs', which scores 0.763 against 'What is our net profit margin after payroll?' -- over the floor, on the shared word 'margin'. The payroll question would then have been handed gross-profit SQL, which is exactly the proxy that produced 'net profit margin after payroll: 67.9%' in Gate 1. The canonical phrasing scores 0.682 and is fine; the alias was the whole of the problem. Measure a new alias against the payroll question before adding it.
